name: Pohnpei Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Pohnpei (eastern caroline islands)
description: Small monarch flycatcher with uniformly dark glossy plumage. Endemic to Pohnpei Island, where it is the only small all-dark bird on the island; male Micronesian Starling is also glossy and dark, but is much larger, with yellow eyes.

name: Green-breasted Pitta
rangeDescription: Cameroon to northern gabon, southwestern central african republic, democratic republic of the congo, and southwestern uganda
description: A spectacular short-tailed upright bird with a distinctive bottle-green breast, a black-and-buff head, a white throat, a scarlet belly, and shiny blue-spotted wings and rump. A scarce resident of dense lowland forest, usually skulking in pairs in leaf litter on the forest floor.

name: Indigo Flowerpiercer
rangeDescription: Andes of western colombia and northwestern ecuador (southward to pichincha)
description: Small flowerpiercer with restricted range in western Colombia and northwest Ecuador. Entirely ultramarine blue, though can appear dark in poor light.

name: Southern Grosbeak-Canary
rangeDescription: Savanna of southern kenya and northeastern tanzania
description: A large seedeater with a very thick pinkish bill. Brownish-olive above and yellow below with streaking along the sides.
imageCreditName: Keith Valentine I Rockjumper Birding Tours

name: Sao Francisco Sparrow
rangeDescription: Eastern brazil (interior of minas gerais and bahia)
description: Handsome, poorly-known sparrow with a bright olive back and a black-and-white face pattern. Note the yellow bill with a black upper ridge.

name: Great Xenops
rangeDescription: Arid caatinga of interior northeastern and east-central brazil
description: Large and subtly beautiful xenops with a pointy curved bill. Has bright rusty plumage with a white throat.

name: Fire-fronted Bishop
rangeDescription: Southwestern somalia to eastern kenya and far northeastern tanzania
description: Breeding males are beautiful and unmistakable, with black-and-yellow plumage and a distinctive red forehead patch. Females and non-breeding males are brown and streaky.

name: Gola Malimbe
rangeDescription: Humid forest of sierra leone, liberia, and southwestern ivory coast
description: A striking black-and-yellow malimbe; the female lacks the yellow nape of the male. Juvenile has a pale bill and yellow on the crown and chin.

name: Anchieta's Sunbird
rangeDescription: Angola to southeastern democratic republic of the congo, zambia, southwestern tanzania, malawi, and northern mozambique
description: Small, distinctive sunbird, red and yellow below with iridescent blue on the forehead, throat, and breast. The male and female are similar, though the female is duller.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Ultramarine Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Marquesas (montane forest of uapou and nukuhiva)
description: A mostly blue-and-white lorikeet with a bright ultramarine upperside and darker blue thighs, chest band, and crown. Chest, throat, cheek, and belly are white with dark flecking.

name: White-cheeked Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of vietnam and southern laos
description: A garrulous, sociable bird, often found in large flocks, both single-species and mixed. Warm brown with a gray crown, a broad black mask, and a luminously white cheek spot, and long white-tipped tail.

name: Chaco Owl
rangeDescription: Chaco of southern bolivia, western paraguay, and northern argentina
description: Large owl of Chaco forest in SE Bolivia, W Paraguay, and NW Argentina. Note round head, barred underparts, and whitish throat.

name: Thick-billed Spiderhunter
rangeDescription: Forest of peninsular thailand, malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Dull and largely unmarked spiderhunter. Brownish olive above with a yellow belly, faint yellow crescents around the eye, and faint speckling on the crown.

name: Subtropical Pygmy-Owl
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of ecuador, peru, and far northern bolivia
description: Rarely encountered owl found in cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes. Small with a round head, yellow eyes, white-speckled crown, and white bands on wings and tail.

name: Yellow-footed Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southern nigeria and cameroon to gabon, democratic republic of the congo, and western uganda; bioko
description: An aptly named flycatcher of the lower parts of the forest edge and forest clearings. Overall grayish with a white belly, a white throat, a uniform gray chest, a mostly yellow bill, and unique bright yellow legs.

name: Slender-billed Parakeet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of chile (aconcagua to northern aysén and chiloé island)
description: Fairly common, but nomadic in the Lake District region of Chile. Found in farmland with forest patches, hedges, and scattered tall trees; less of a forest bird than the smaller and duller Austral Parakeet, although the two species rarely if ever mix together.

name: Firethroat
rangeDescription: Mountains of southeastern tibet to west-central china; winters to northeastern myanmar
description: Male is stunning, with a metallic blue back, a black mask extending down to the shoulder, and a burning flame-orange throat and breast. Female is plain brown and very difficult to distinguish from female Indian Blue Robin (which generally breeds at lower altitudes than Firethroat) and Siberian Blue Robin (which overlaps with Firethroat only on migration); look out for the female Firethroat’s relatively brighter white throat, darker underparts, and lack of scaling on the breast.

name: Gilolo Fantail
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (halmahera, ternate, bacan, and obi)
description: Small, active songbird with long, pale-tipped tail and warm brownish-orange on the forehead, rump, and tail base. Grayish brown above and pale below overall, with a white throat and black-speckled breast.

name: Slaty-backed Thornbill
rangeDescription: Mulga areas of central western australia to south-central queensland
description: Small bird with thin pointed bill, uncommon in mulga woodland of arid inland temperate Australia. Brownish gray above, cream-colored below, with dark eye, dark streaking on forecrown, pale lores, pale-tipped dark tail, and chestnut rump, often visible in flight.

name: Schrenck's Bittern
rangeDescription: Eastern asia; winters to southeastern asia, philippines, and greater sundas
description: Small heron, usually found in reed beds, expansive marshes, and rice fields; can occasionally be found in parks with sheltered areas, particularly lotus ponds and shaded pools. Generally uncommon throughout its range; never in the high densities of Yellow Bittern.
